llm.summary: The package mostly matches its stated purpose (API DB + lint/chat helpers) but contains inconsistencies and hard-coded filesystem paths that warrant caution before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with provided files: an API database, a chatbot/search tool, and a linter. The provided scripts implement the advertised features (search, interactive/web chatbot, lint). However there are filename mismatches between scripts and included JSON (see detail) which indicate sloppy packaging.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs running the provided scripts which is within purpose. But two auxiliary scripts (extract_functions.py and parse_api_data.py) contain hard-coded input paths pointing at /root/.openclaw/qqbot/downloads/... — i.e., agent/user-specific locations outside the skill's domain. If a user runs those scripts as-is they will attempt to read files from that path. The runtime instructions do not mention these hard-coded paths or any need to access agent config/download directories.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; instruction-only runtime. No remote downloads or package installs specified. Risk from install mechanism is low.

dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or credentials, which is appropriate. But scripts access local filesystem (including the hard-coded /root/.openclaw path). That gives the code potential to read local files outside the repo if run without inspection. This is not declared in SKILL.md and is disproportionate to a simple lint/search tool.

dimensions.detail: No special persistence/privileges requested (always:false). The skill does write output files only when running extractor scripts, but it does not modify other skills or agent config in the manifest.

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement a Virtuoso Skill API database, a chatbot search, and a linter — which matches its description — but there are a few red flags you should consider before running anything: 1) Filename inconsistencies: the chatbot and linter expect different JSON filenames (e.g., skill_chatbot.py defaults to 'skill_api_database.json' while the repo provides 'references/skill_api_database.json' and the linter expects 'skill_api_database_full.json'). That will cause runtime errors unless you rename or adjust paths. 2) Hard-coded paths: the helper scripts extract_functions.py and parse_api_data.py contain hard-coded input_path values under /root/.openclaw/qqbot/downloads/… If executed unchanged they will try to read files from that agent/user directory. Although the code only parses local files (no network calls), it could read sensitive local content if those paths exist. 3) No network exfiltration code was found, but the ability to read arbitrary local files is present if you run the extractor/parse scripts. Recommendations: - Inspect the JSON database file in 'references/' to confirm it contains only the API data you expect. - Do not run extract_functions.py or parse_api_data.py unless you review and edit the hard-coded paths; run them in a sandbox or container. - If you want to use the chatbot or linter, either rename the included JSON to the filenames the scripts expect or update the scripts to point to the local reference file. - Prefer running the linter/chatbot locally in a restricted environment, and avoid running scripts as root. If you want, I can list exact lines with hard-coded paths and suggest safe edits to make before running.
